claims.text: Single-pass SLM CoCrFeNiMn components typically contain residual porosity.
Single-pass SLM CoCrFeNiMn components typically exhibit microstructural inhomogeneities.
Rapid melting and solidification cause dimensional distortions in SLM CoCrFeNiMn components.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will reduce fabrication-induced defects in SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will improve the dimensional precision of SLM CoCrFeNiMn components.
An in-situ laser remelting pass after every deposited layer will improve the mechanical integrity of SLM CoCrFeNiMn components.
A remelting pass operated at approximately 70–80% of the primary laser power is expected to be effective under standard inert-atmosphere SLM conditions.
Laser remelting promotes chemical or microstructural homogenization.
Laser remelting reduces porosity and eliminates minor defects in SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
Laser remelting refines the grain structure of SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
Laser remelting improves interlayer bonding in SLM CoCrFeNiMn.
Remelting gives pores and micro-cracks an opportunity to heal.
Controlled solidification of the remelted layer reduces residual thermal stresses.
Defect healing and reduced residual thermal stress produce a more uniform structure with fewer dimensional distortions.
A more uniform structure and fewer dimensional distortions translate into improved mechanical properties.
Relative to single-pass SLM, layer-by-layer remelting will reduce porosity and dimensional deviations.
Relative to single-pass SLM, layer-by-layer remelting will enhance tensile strength and ductility.
The intervention's efficacy may vary across alloy systems and substantially altered build parameters.
